title: [decision] Freeze the stage-1 action menu before round 0
description:
The menus in section 2.1 (intervals {0, 0.5, 1, 2, 4}, mode {0.5, 1, 2}, restart margin {0.5, 1, 2}, sweep effort {0, 0.5, 1, 2}), one-shot m = 0, the 0.1 floor and the masking. Labels are over menu entries, so the menu cannot change after round 0 without discarding data. Use the step-0 effect sizes to prune entries that never win.

Plan: section 2.1, section 6.4 'Invariants across rounds'.
acceptance_criteria: Menu recorded in the plan's decision log with the date; the SAT_POLICY_BRANCH_ACTIONS defaults match.

title: [decision] Decision epoch X_d: 2^26, 2^27 or 2^28
description:
Default 2^27 (decision 2026-09-14): about 4-6 s, about 25 k conflicts on a typical cell, spanning about 3 stock probe fires. The decision epoch is also the segment a fork child holds. Choose from the tier-2 sweep and freeze before round 0, since labels are over one-epoch deviations.

Plan: section 1, section 6.3, section 6.4 'Invariants across rounds'.
acceptance_criteria: Value recorded here and in the plan's decision log; the SAT_POLICY_EPOCH_TICKS default updated if it changes.

title: [B.11] Family-stratified validation split of sat-comp-2025
description:
About 100 cells drawn stratified by family from the 400, held out of all fitting and used only for checkpoint selection. Commit the split file with the seed and the per-family counts. Every training script must read it and refuse to fit on validation cells.

Plan: section 8 'Splits'.
acceptance_criteria: Split file committed; per-family counts in the bead; the tools/rl/ training code asserts the exclusion.

title: [B.10] Run: X_d sweep on tier 2
description:
Compare decision epochs 2^26, 2^27 and 2^28 (observation epoch fixed at 2^23) on the tier-2 cells: how many stock timer fires each epoch spans per cell, decisions per run, logging and decide overhead, and the size of the paired difference a one-epoch deviation produces in random mode. Feeds the X_d decision bead; the menu and the epoch must be frozen before round 0.

Plan: section 1, section 10 step B.
acceptance_criteria: Table per X_d in the decision bead; run directory recorded.

title: [B.9] Normalization and the static-feature runtime predictor
description:
Fit mean and std per feature on the 2025 training-split traces and write them in the weights-file format the solver reads. Train the static-feature runtime predictor (critic baseline and feature sanity check) and report its validation error per family.

Plan: section 3, section 5.2, section 6.2 item 3 'diagnostic'.
acceptance_criteria: Normalization file loads in the solver; predictor error reported in the bead and the README.

title: [B.7] tools/rl_dataset.py: log-to-table converter
description:
One-time, resumable, one run at a time: raw log rows to a compact per-decision feature table (parquet) with counter deltas, pairing to the stock run at the same ticks, censoring flags, flavour and branch bookkeeping. The compact tables (a few MB per run) fit in memory for training; the raw logs are tens of GB compressed at fork scale.

Plan: section 7 item 7, section 12 'Log volume'.
acceptance_criteria: Converts the 2025 stock traces end to end; re-running skips finished runs; a unit test on a fixture log checks the deltas.

title: [B.6] Per-cell tables: B_cell, peak RSS, family labels
description:
Build one table the collector and the evaluation scripts read: B_cell = the work clock W the stock run had reached at clamp(3 x stock solve time, 120 s, 1800 s) of its own wall (whole suite) or at 3600 s (band); peak RSS per cell; the critic-tier family label; SAT/UNSAT label and stock solve time.

Plan: sections 3.4, 5.4, 7 item 6d.
acceptance_criteria: Table committed under benchmarks/ or tools/rl/ with provenance (log directory, date); a script regenerates it from the logs.

title: [B.5] Fit k_res and the wall weights per work kind
description:
From the stock traces, regress wall per row on the per-row deltas of each work kind (search ticks, probing ticks, kitten ticks, sweep, vivify, backbone, factor and transitive ticks, walk flips, eliminate resolutions). k_res is the eliminate-resolution weight relative to a tick; the other weights are the reward's dense-cost weights. Bake k_res into the one constant the TSV tooling and SAT_LIMIT_TICKS read, and record the fit (residuals per family) in the solver README. Without wall calibration a policy could shift work into cheap-unit passes.

Plan: sections 3.4, 4, 14 item 2.
acceptance_criteria: k_res and the weights committed with the fit report; feature_ablation.py, the run_kissat_full.sh tooling and the solver constant agree; the tick-limit determinism test still passes.

title: [B.3] Run: stock traces on sat-comp-2026 (400 cells, holdout, 1800 s)
description:
Same as B.2 on the 2026 track. These traces are for evaluation only: the paired stock reference when the holdout is run, and a sanity check of feature ranges. They never enter normalization, fitting or selection.

Plan: sections 5.2 and 8.
acceptance_criteria: 400 logs; directory recorded; a note in the bead that no fitting script reads this directory.

title: [B.4] Run: stock traces for the timeout band at 3600 s
description:
The cells stock could not solve at 1800 s (about 90) rerun at 3600 s, twice the gate. This defines B_cell on the band and gives terminal signal on cells the policy might rescue.

Plan: section 5.4, section 4 'Larger-than-budget instances', section 13 item 2.
acceptance_criteria: Band membership list and logs recorded; B_cell for the band computed from these traces.

title: [B.2] Run: stock traces on sat-comp-2025 (400 cells, 1800 s)
description:
Stock solver 13 with SAT_POLICY=stock and logging on, one pass, proofs off, 1800 s wall. This is the paired reference for every later comparison and the source of normalization, behaviour-cloning targets and B_cell. Check for live sweeps first, launch detached, and record the log directory and PID here.

Plan: section 5.2, section 5.4 table.
acceptance_criteria: 400 logs with headers and footers (peak RSS); log directory recorded in this bead and in the solver README; zero correctness failures.

title: [B.1] tools/rl_collect.py: the collection harness
description:
feature_ablation.py knows nothing about fork children. The collector needs: process-group accounting so a killed run takes its children; jobs = parents x (1 + children) under the 32-process cap; per-child memory caps from the cell's peak RSS; per-cell tick budgets (SAT_LIMIT_TICKS = B_cell) with a generous wall cap logged as an anomaly, not a result; seed and flavour bookkeeping (every run uses the paired stock run's seed); a manifest per pass; resumability. It asserts that every parent and child of one branch point that finishes reports the same SAT/UNSAT and validates every child's SAT model (a disagreement is a solver bug and stops the run). Proofs off.

Plan: sections 5.3, 5.4, 7 items 6c, 6d and 7, 15 item 6.
acceptance_criteria: A small run on benchmarks/discriminating with 1 parent and a few children per cell produces a manifest and all logs and passes the sibling-agreement check; killing the run leaves no orphan solver processes.

title: [B] Collector, stock traces, work-clock constants and the validation split
description:
The data foundation: a collector that understands fork children and tick budgets; stock traces of solver 13 with logging on the 2025 and 2026 suites and the timeout band; the fitted constants (k_res and the wall weights per work kind); per-cell budgets B_cell; the log-to-table converter; the critic-tier features; normalization and the runtime predictor; the X_d sweep; and the validation split.

Plan: sections 5.2, 5.4, 7 item 7, 10 step B.
acceptance_criteria: Stock traces for 2025, 2026 and the band exist with recorded log directories; k_res and the wall weights are fitted and baked into the tooling; B_cell, peak RSS and family tables exist per cell; the validation split file is committed; the X_d decision is recorded.
notes: Cost from the plan: 1-2 suite passes (about 10 h for 2025 + 2026, about 3 h for the band).

title: [A.12] Document the env contract and the conventions for policy code
description:
Add the table of SAT_POLICY, SAT_POLICY_LOG, SAT_POLICY_EPOCH_TICKS, SAT_POLICY_TEMP, SAT_POLICY_SEED, SAT_POLICY_MARGIN, SAT_POLICY_BRANCH, SAT_POLICY_BRANCH_ACTIONS, SAT_POLICY_HORIZON, SAT_WALL_LIMIT, SAT_LIMIT_TICKS and SAT_EXTRA_ARGS to solver/13-kissat-rs/README.md. Add the policy rules to CONVENTIONS.md: chokepoints are two-line 'if policy.on' branches; observe() and log_row() are pure; new counters stay out of the -s block; k_res lives in one place.

Plan: section 7 items 6 and 6e.
acceptance_criteria: README and CONVENTIONS.md updated; a new agent can run a random-mode logged run from the README alone.

title: [A.11] Overhead check: policy-on-STOCK with logging v policy-off
description:
Before collecting 800 traces, measure what logging, snapshots and observe() cost. Two arms on sat-comp-2025-medium with feature_ablation.py: stock (policy off) and policy-on with the stock action and SAT_POLICY_LOG on. Report wall and W per cell. W must be identical per cell (that is the parity claim) and the wall overhead should be small. Quiet host for the wall numbers. Record log paths in the solver README.

Plan: section 8 'Gate arms', section 7 item 6e.
acceptance_criteria: W identical per cell across the two arms; wall geomean overhead recorded; anything over a few percent gets a profiling bead.

title: [A.10] Net loader, forward pass and the margin over stock
description:
SAT_POLICY=path loads a flat little-endian f32 file (shapes, normalization, weights). Hand-rolled MLP forward in Rust, no new crates: trunk 150 -> 128 -> 64 with ReLU, one head per knob (five 5-way interval heads, mode 3-way, restart margin 3-way, sweep effort 4-way). Act on a non-stock entry only when its score beats the stock entry by SAT_POLICY_MARGIN (log-odds; an infinite margin must be stock). Invalid entries are masked to stock. Keep the build generic x86-64 and never rely on FMA contraction. Leave room in the file format for per-knob tree or linear rankers, which may win the deploy-target decision.

Plan: section 6.4, section 7 item 8, section 6.1 step 4.
acceptance_criteria: Forward pass matches a PyTorch reference on a fixed weights file to 1e-6 (test in tools/rl/ plus a Rust fixture); infinite margin passes parity 20/20; inference cost measured once and recorded (expected negligible at 2^27).

title: [A.9] observe(): the feature vector with multi-scale deltas and the horizon
description:
Build the roughly 150-float input from the last 16 snapshots and the static block: global dynamics as deltas over the last 1, 4 and 16 observation epochs (zero-filled with a validity flag per window until enough snapshots exist), the per-timer block (log stock delta, progress, fire count, would-fire), the per-pass recency block, and the horizon (fraction of budget used): elapsed wall over SAT_WALL_LIMIT at inference, ticks over the limit under SAT_LIMIT_TICKS, and SAT_POLICY_HORIZON=ticks:B for parity and replay. Counts as log1p, sizes as ratios; normalization constants come from the weights file. Must be pure with respect to solver state.

Plan: sections 3.1-3.4, 6.4, 7 item 6e.
acceptance_criteria: observe() output for a logged run can be recomputed offline from the log rows to the same floats (test on a fixture); parity 20/20 with observe running every decision.

title: [A.7] Actor-tier static features next to classify()
description:
One pass over active variables and non-garbage clauses after preprocessing: shape (vars, clauses, literals, clause-length histogram, giant-clause share), occurrence and polarity moments, Horn fractions, binary-implication-graph degrees and binary fraction, locality (clause span over vars), SCC count and sizes from substitute's walk, the congruence gate census, backbone and sweep yields with budget-hit flags, kitten counts, fast-elimination counts, lucky outcome per pattern, warmup assigned fraction, preprocessing ticks by pass, and a bounded BFS implication depth and reach from a sample of literals (sample size by standard error, edge visits capped at about 1 M). Dumped in the log header and available to D0. Locality is not shuffle-invariant; keep the groups separable so ablations can mask them.

Plan: sections 2.4, 3.5, 3.6, Appendix A.
acceptance_criteria: Costs at most about 0.5x parse time on the giant cells (Kakuro, brocard); zero effect on search counters (parity 20/20); every group is named in the header so tools can mask it.

title: [A.8] Fork mode: branch children at decision points
description:
SAT_POLICY_BRANCH=schedule and SAT_POLICY_BRANCH_ACTIONS. At a branch point the process forks one child per alternative menu entry of one knob. Each child holds its entry for one decision epoch, then returns control to the parent's policy, stops on its own tick budget (B_cell, or twice it on the timeout band), and logs to its own file named after the parent log, the branch point and the child index with stdout and stderr redirected so the harness never sees a second 's' line. The parent blocks on a semaphore until a child slot frees (costs wall, not ticks). Hygiene: flush stdout, stderr and the log writer before fork; the child reopens its own files; the RNG state is inherited on purpose; refuse to fork while a proof file is open. Solver 13 is single-threaded and libc is already a dependency.

Plan: section 5.3 flavour 1, section 7 item 6c, section 15 items 3 and 4.
acceptance_criteria: Test: a child with act == STOCK matches the parent's counters at the same tick; no duplicated output after fork; fork refused with a proof file open; cargo test and the smoke test pass.

title: [A.5] Logger: raw state every observation epoch plus a header and footer
description:
SAT_POLICY_LOG=path. Every observation epoch write all statistics counters as raw u64, both averages blocks, every limit, the delay counters, the elimination bound, the tier glue limits, mode, level, trail, unassigned, arena and garbage sizes, the per-epoch learned-clause histogram, the stock counterfactual (deadline and would-fire per timer), the action in force, the policy RNG state and the monotonic wall clock. The header carries the static features (A.7) and the run's configuration; the footer carries the result and peak RSS from getrusage. Row width is free (about 35 MB per run raw); choose a compact binary or columnar format the converter (B.7) reads. log_row must be pure: no RNG draws, no allocation that changes the arena, no counter that feeds a heuristic.

Plan: section 5.1, section 7 items 1, 6d and 6e.
acceptance_criteria: policy-on-STOCK with logging passes parity 20/20; a 1800 s run's log is under about 50 MB; the converter can rebuild every counter delta from the rows.

title: [A.6] Counter audit: re-enable the compiled-out METRIC counters
description:
The port compiles out about 40 kissat METRIC counters as no-ops (literals learned, minimized, shrunken, bumped, deduced; definitions checked and extracted; walk decisions; target and best saved; rescaled, compacted, flushed). Re-enable the ones the observation needs. They are pure increments and cannot change search. Keep every re-enabled counter out of the -s block or behind a flag, because parity.py compares every -s counter against the C. Complete raw logging is an invariant across rounds (features may change later and old rounds are re-derived), so err on the side of logging more.

Plan: section 5.1, section 7 item 5, section 12 item 7, section 13 item 5.
acceptance_criteria: List of re-enabled counters in the solver README; parity.py 20/20 unchanged; search-bound wall on benchmarks/discriminating within noise of before (cache-resident cells, idle host).

title: [A.4] Random mode and the replay test
description:
SAT_POLICY=random with SAT_POLICY_TEMP and SAT_POLICY_SEED. Two flavours: segmented sticky (geometric segment lengths with a mean of about 5 decision epochs; at each segment start the action is STOCK with probability 0.5, else each knob is drawn from a categorical centred on 1 with the run's temperature) and near-stock jitter (per-decision resampling at low temperature). m = 0 gets a small probability (about 0.05) so wild runs do not fire every timer every few epochs. The policy's RNG is its own, never the solver's.

Plan: section 5.3 flavours 2 and 3, section 12 item 8.
acceptance_criteria: A seeded random run replays to identical counters (test); the solver's own RNG stream is unchanged by the policy (parity with act == STOCK still 20/20).

title: [A.3] Stage-1 chokepoints: six fire predicates, restart margin, sweep effort
description:
Each chokepoint is a two-line 'if policy.on' branch. due(T) for probe, eliminate, reduce, rephase, reorder and mode uses last_fire + m x stock_delta with a floor of 0.1 x stock_delta. m = 0 is one-shot: fire once at the next safe point, then behave as 1 until the next decision. The restartmargin read is scaled in focused mode only. The sweep permille effort is multiplied (0 skips the round; stock DELAYING(sweep) stays ANDed). Stock's update_conflict_limit math is untouched.

Plan: sections 2.1, 2.3, 7 item 2, 15 item 1.
acceptance_criteria: parity.py 20/20 policy-on with act == STOCK; a unit test that last_fire + 1 x stock_delta equals limits[T] after every fire; a test that m = 0 fires exactly once per decision epoch.

title: [A.2] src/policy.rs core: state, epoch clock, action, search-loop hook
description:
Create the module. Policy state: observation and decision epoch counters on search_ticks (X_o = 2^23 and X_d = 2^27 by default, SAT_POLICY_EPOCH_TICKS=X_o,X_d); mode from SAT_POLICY=stock, random, or a weights file path; the Action struct (six interval multipliers, restart margin, eight effort multipliers, elimination-bound choice, reduce fraction) with STOCK = all ones; per-timer stock_delta and last_fire bookkeeping where init_conflict_limit and every fire store the stock delta; masking of invalid actions (rephase in focused, restart margin in stable, reorder per mode). The hook goes at the head of the search-loop if-chain (src/search.rs): log_row every X_o, decide every X_d and at D0 (search_ticks = 0, before the first decide).

Plan: sections 1, 2.1, 2.3, 2.4 (D0), 7 items 1 and 3.
acceptance_criteria: Policy off: no added line executes on the search path beyond one branch; parity.py 20/20 policy-off; cargo test covers the epoch arithmetic and the masking.

title: [A.1] SAT_LIMIT_TICKS: a deterministic work-clock limit
description:
The solver has only --conflicts and --decisions. Add a limited.ticks alongside them: stop with 's UNKNOWN' when the work clock W = statistics.ticks + k_res x eliminate_resolutions reaches the limit. Check it where the conflict limit is checked and inside the inprocessing effort loops, so a long eliminate or sweep cannot overrun by much. k_res is one constant in one place (provisional until step B fits it). Every perturbed run and every tick-deterministic comparison depends on this.

Plan: section 7 item 6b, section 3.4, section 14 item 1.
acceptance_criteria: Two runs of the same cell with the same limit stop at identical counters (test); the limit is honoured within one inprocessing pass of the target; unset leaves behaviour byte-identical; the smoke test passes.

title: [A] Solver plumbing: policy module, chokepoints, logger, fork, tick limit
description:
Everything the solver itself needs. Additive and off by default: with the policy off no added line executes and parity with the C stays exact; with the policy on and the stock action every fire predicate equals the stock value. src/policy.rs does not exist yet; this step creates it. Read solver/13-kissat-rs/CONVENTIONS.md (binding) and plan sections 2, 3, 5.1, 5.3 and 7 before starting.

Plan: section 7, section 10 step A.
acceptance_criteria: tools/parity.py 20/20 at 100 k conflicts policy-off and policy-on-STOCK; cargo test and the smoke test pass; every SAT_POLICY_* and SAT_LIMIT_TICKS knob is documented in the solver README.
notes: Cost from the plan: 2-3 sessions, not 1.

title: [0.5] Headroom estimate and per-knob effect sizes

From the sweeps: for each knob, how often and by how much a non-stock constant beats stock (per family and overall); the best global constant per knob; and the total headroom if every cell got its best constant, an upper bound the epoch policy must beat. Write it into solver/13-kissat-rs/README.md with log paths and machine metadata, and into the plan's decision log. The effect sizes weight the round-0 branch points and start knob triage.

One line: append the contents of SAT_EXTRA_ARGS (word-split) to the sat-solver command in both run.sh paths. Empty or unset must be byte-identical to today. Document it in the solver README and note that the parity oracle is unaffected. Example: SAT_EXTRA_ARGS='--eliminateint=1000'.

title: [A'.2] feature_ablation.py: W per cell and tick PAR-2
description:
Parse the exit line into the per-cell results TSV as ticks, eliminate_resolutions and W, with k_res read from one constant in one place (provisional value, refit in step B). title: [A'.3] run_kissat_full.sh results.csv and compare_full_runs.py: W and tick PAR-2
description:

The C kissat arm never prints statistics.ticks, so for that arm record what -s offers (search and probing ticks, eliminate resolutions) and mark W as unavailable rather than inventing it. title: [G] Evaluation discipline for every RL gate
description:
The rules every comparison and gate in this project follows. Gate beads link here. Re-read before launching one.

- Three arms every time: stock (policy off), policy-on with the stock action (measures logging and inference overhead alone), and the candidate.
- Metric order: solved instances, then tick PAR-2 on the work clock W (never search_ticks), then wall PAR-2. Report per family.
- Splits: sat-comp-2025 (400) and the medium suite (100, fully inside 2025) are training data. A family-stratified validation split of about 100 cells from 2025 is held out of all fitting and used for checkpoint selection. sat-comp-2026 is the true holdout and is run at most once per promoted candidate (solver 12 lesson: 296 v 292 on 2025, 160 v 197 on 2026).
- Choose what to gate with tick-budgeted deterministic runs (SAT_LIMIT_TICKS = B_cell). Only wall runs are promotion evidence. Plus or minus 2 solved is noise on 100 cells, so the 400-cell wall run plus the deterministic comparison are the decision evidence; the medium gate stays the repo's formal promotion gate.
- Promoted candidates are also run on variable-renamed, clause-shuffled copies of the validation split. A win that disappears under shuffle is input-order luck and does not count. Locality features are the most exposed.
- Correctness is absolute: a wrong answer, an invalid model, a missing or invalid proof, or a premature UNKNOWN fails the gate with no trade. Fork siblings must agree on SAT/UNSAT.
- Resource cap: at most 32 solver processes and 16 GB per process; paired arms split the cores; marginal wall timing is invalid while another sweep runs. Check for live processes before launching.

Plan: sections 4 and 8. CLAUDE.md: 'Evaluation' and 'Correctness is absolute'.
acceptance_criteria: Stays open for the life of the project. Every gate bead links here with a related dependency, and its result records all three arms per family.

title: RL scheduler for solver 13: learn when to run inprocessing and how hard to restart
description:
Solver 13 is a faithful Rust port of kissat 4.0.4. This project replaces only its timing layer: when to run probe, eliminate, reduce, rephase, reorder and the mode switch, how aggressive restarts are, and later how much effort each pass gets. A small model is consulted once every fixed number of search ticks. Every mechanism stays byte-identical, and with the policy off the solver stays at exact parity with the C.

Work order (plan section 10): A' (work-clock ticks in the harness tables), 0 (constant-knob baseline sweeps), A (solver plumbing), B (collector and stock traces), C (round-0 perturbation dataset), D (baselines and the stock clone), E (ranking policy, DAgger rounds, gates, holdout), F (stage 2). Each step is a child epic here. Decision beads hold the choices the plan leaves to data. The governance bead holds the evaluation rules every gate must follow. The parking-lot epic holds ideas the plan parks.

Metric, in order: solved instances, tick PAR-2 on the work clock W = statistics.ticks + k_res x eliminate_resolutions, then wall PAR-2. Correctness is absolute.

Fork stock plus every entry within a band of the best; saved children become more branch points. Concentrate on the top 3-4 knobs from triage.

The restart test itself (fires every ~30 conflicts) stays stock in this plan; only the margin regime is a knob. If the epoch policy's restart-margin head shows a large effect, a learned per-conflict test is the follow-up. Literature: Haim and Walsh 2009 restart strategy selection; bandit-based restart and branching switches in MapleSAT-era solvers and Kissat_MAB.

Plan: section 13 'Beyond the current purview'.
acceptance_criteria: Only after stage 1 shows a large restart-margin effect.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] Publish the stock-trace dataset and what it shows on the site
description:
Epoch-level traces of stock solver 13 on 800 instances with wall per row answer questions beyond RL: where wall goes per family, which passes are barren on which structures, how ticks per second varies with formula shape. Worth a page under docs/ once the traces exist. Conventions: docs/SITE_WORKFLOW.md; use the debug-web-visualizations skill for anything visual.

Plan: section 13 'Beyond the current purview'.
acceptance_criteria: A page on the site built from the stock traces, following docs/SITE_WORKFLOW.md.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] At-most-one clique census as an actor feature
description:
Count cliques of mutually exclusive literals on the binary implication graph. These are at-most-one constraints from 'pick one value' encodings (planning, timetabling, colouring, Kakuro, pigeonhole). Greedy clique growth with a cap; it can blow up on dense graphs, so it is bounded and deferred.

Plan: section 3.6 and Appendix A.
acceptance_criteria: A bounded implementation with measured cost on the giant cells and an ablation showing it helps.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] Adaptive epoch length for giant cells
description:
A fixed epoch first. Ticks per conflict spans about 50x across cells, so a typical cell sees about 1500 conflicts per decision epoch and brocard about 35. If a fixed epoch fails on such cells, scale X by the ticks per conflict measured in the first epochs.

Plan: section 9.
acceptance_criteria: Only if the fixed-epoch policy is shown to fail on the giant-cell regime.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] Initial-walk probe as an actor feature
description:
Run kissat's walkinitially once before search under walkeffort and feed the policy the minimum unsatisfied-clause count reached and how fast it fell. SATzilla found local-search features among the most predictive of satisfiability. It changes stock behaviour (turns on a pass and sets saved phases), so it goes in only if a fork-at-parse counterfactual shows the information is worth its ticks.

Plan: section 3.6 and Appendix A.
acceptance_criteria: A fork-at-parse measurement showing the feature pays for its ticks.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] Shuffled copies as training augmentation
description:
Train on variable-renamed, clause-shuffled copies of training cells to reduce dependence on input order and locality. Parked 2026-09-14 as a later experiment if extra margin is needed. Shuffled copies are already used at evaluation (see the governance bead).

Plan: sections 13 and 8.
acceptance_criteria: A validation comparison with and without the augmentation.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] PPO fallback if fork labels stop improving while outcomes show headroom
description:
The plan chose DAgger-with-fork over PPO: about 10 passes give at most 8 PPO updates, its exploration is uninformed sampling, and it cannot use exact replay or same-state counterfactuals, the two things this setting has that most RL settings lack. Revisit only if the DAgger rounds stall while the outcome data still shows headroom.

Plan: section 6.2 item 4.
acceptance_criteria: Only if the go/no-go decision after a DAgger round names PPO as the next try.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] D-1: let the policy control preprocessing rounds and effort
description:
A stage-2 head that chooses preprocessrounds and applies effort multipliers to the preprocessing round's passes, before lucky and before D0. Data would come from fork-at-parse children with different rounds and effort from the identical parsed state, the cheapest counterfactual in the design. Skipped for now (decision 2026-09-12): D0's strongest inputs are the preprocessing yields, which depend on what D-1 chose. Section 2.4 says how to handle that if it is adopted (menu {1, 2} first, D0 observes the D-1 action, D0 trained first and frozen while D-1 data is collected). Reopen through the decision bead 'Adopt D-1'.

Plan: sections 2.4 and 9.
acceptance_criteria: Reopened only by the D-1 decision bead; then split into solver, collector and training tasks.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parked] Offline RL side line (IQL or AWR) on the sticky and jitter flavours
description:
Train an offline-RL learner on all perturbation flavours, using the sticky segments for multi-step credit, with a discount per tick over a horizon of about the budget. Checkpoints chosen on the validation split, never on training loss. The main line has no critic and uses fork-sibling ranking instead. Worth a run only if the ranking learner plateaus with headroom left.

Plan: section 6.2 item 3, section 4 'Discount'.
acceptance_criteria: A validation comparison against the ranking policy of the same round.
notes: Parked by the plan; reopen only when the main line gives a reason.

title: [parking lot] Ideas the plan parks for later
description: Ideas the plan records but deliberately does not schedule. Each child is deferred. Reopen one only when the main line gives a reason: a plateau, a measured need, or spare host time. Rejected ideas (learned choices inside passes, curriculum training) are not here; the plan's section 13 records why they were rejected.
acceptance_criteria: Holds deferred children only.
